title: AHB Family Comparison
description: Open each variant to compare master context, arbitration, responses, security, exclusives, and typical deployment.

signals.name: Original AHB
signals.description: The original protocol includes shared-bus arbitration and legacy SPLIT/RETRY responses so multiple masters can contend directly for one bus.
signals.direction: Multiple masters and slaves share one arbitrated bus
signals.sampled: Transfers remain synchronous to HCLK; grant ownership controls which master may drive
signals.verificationNote: Track grant ownership, locked sequences, and SPLIT/RETRY re-arbitration; do not apply AHB-Lite response rules.

signals.name: AHB-Lite
signals.description: AHB-Lite removes bus-level multi-master arbitration and legacy SPLIT/RETRY responses. A bus matrix can still combine several independent single-master interfaces.
signals.direction: One master per interface; a matrix arbitrates internally when needed
signals.sampled: Address/control are accepted on a rising HCLK edge when HREADY is HIGH
signals.typicalUse: Most contemporary microcontroller IP and subsystem buses
signals.verificationNote: Do not expect shared-bus grant signals. Check that ERROR uses the AHB-Lite two-cycle response sequence.

signals.name: AHB5
signals.description: AHB5 keeps the AHB-Lite transfer model while adding modern memory attributes, security signaling, and exclusive-access support.
signals.direction: Single-master interfaces connected through modern interconnects
signals.sampled: Base control plus AHB5 attributes are sampled with the accepted address phase
signals.typicalUse: Secure IoT, automotive, and current microcontroller SoCs
signals.verificationNote: Keep security, exclusive success, and ordinary HRESP semantics separate; HEXOKAY=0 is not itself an ERROR.
